findings.title: Pause and Delete menu items can never render without a ruler rule
findings.body: The menu now computes `canPause`/`canDelete` from the Prometheus-rule abilities as well (so that the list view works without ruler requests), but the render conditions are still `canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` (line 123) and `canDelete && rulerRule` (line 165). In the new rule list view `rulerRule` is `undefined` (GrafanaRuleListItem only passes `promRule`), so Pause/Unpause and Delete can never be shown there. The newly added ability plumbing for those two actions is dead code and users lose the ability to pause or delete a rule from the list, which the GrafanaGroupLoader test now bakes in by asserting exactly 4 menu items.

findings.title: Silence menu item is a no-op when only a Prometheus rule is provided
findings.body: `AlertRuleMenu` now shows the "Silence notifications" item based on the Prometheus-rule abilities, so it appears in the list view where only `promRule` is passed. However the drawer is still rendered conditionally on `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` (line 104), and `rule` (the ruler rule) is `undefined` in that path. Clicking "Silence notifications" sets `showSilenceDrawer` but nothing ever renders, so the action silently does nothing for every rule in the new list view.

findings.title: skipToken path returns permissive abilities instead of all-false
findings.body: `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility`/`useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` map `skipToken` to `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined)` rather than short-circuiting. With `rule === undefined`, `loading` is false so `MaybeSupported` becomes `AlwaysSupported`, and abilities built with `toAbility` (Duplicate at line 318, View, Explore) come back as `[true, ctx.hasPermission(...)]`. Since `AlertRuleMenu` ORs the ruler-based and prom-based abilities, a data-source (e.g. Mimir) rule — which passes `skipToken` — is reported as duplicatable for anyone holding the global Grafana `alert.rule:create` permission, even when the ruler-based check says the action isn't supported. The skip path should return all-`[false,false]` abilities.

findings.title: OR-ing ruler and prom abilities lets the more permissive source win
findings.body: Every ability is combined as `(rulerSupported && rulerAllowed) || (promSupported && promAllowed)` (lines 83-100). The ruler-based hook deliberately marks a rule as not supported when it is immutable (provisioned, plugin-provided, federated); the prom-based hook detects provisioning only through the brand-new optional `provenance` field on `GrafanaPromRuleDTO`. Whenever that field is absent from the Prometheus response (it is typed optional and nothing guarantees the backend sends it), the prom branch reports Pause/Delete/Duplicate as allowed and the OR overrides the ruler branch's immutability guard, exposing destructive actions for provisioned rules that the API will reject. Consider selecting one source per call site rather than OR-ing, and/or treating an absent `provenance` conservatively.

findings.title: Missing React `key` on GrafanaRuleListItem in the filtered list
findings.body: The grafana branch of the `rules.map(...)` switch previously rendered `<GrafanaRuleLoader key={key} ... />`; the replacement `<GrafanaRuleListItem ... />` (lines 157-163) dropped the `key` prop while the datasource and unknown branches still pass it. This produces React key warnings and, because the filter view appends pages incrementally, can cause incorrect element reuse/re-mounting (losing per-item state such as an open menu) as new batches are concatenated.

findings.title: Federated rule-group protection removed for all consumers of useAllAlertRuleAbilities
findings.body: `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` now delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, where `isFederated` is hardcoded to `false` (line 245, with only a TODO). Previously it called `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)`, which made Update/Delete/Pause unsupported for Mimir federated rule groups. With this change the existing (non-list) rule views will offer Edit/Delete on federated groups, leading to user-visible failures or unintended modifications of groups that cannot be edited through this UI.

findings.title: Pause/ModifyExport incorrectly restricted to alerting rules for Grafana prom rules
findings.body: In `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, `AlertRuleAction.Pause` (line 325), `Restore`, `DeletePermanently` and `ModifyExport` (line 324) are gated on `isAlertingRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`. The ruler-based equivalent used `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule`, which includes Grafana-managed *recording* rules. Grafana-managed recording rules do support pausing (`is_paused`) and export, so this hook reports those actions as unsupported for them, hiding valid functionality once the list view relies on this hook.

findings.title: Rule view link no longer carries `returnTo`
findings.body: The deleted `GrafanaRuleLoader` built the href as `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })` using `createReturnTo()`. The new component drops the `returnTo` query parameter (line 40), so navigating from the rule list into a rule detail page loses the "return to previous" context and the back affordance in the detail view will no longer point at the filtered list the user came from.

findings.title: Stale comment and variable name after removing ruler prefetch
findings.body: The ruler `getGrafanaRulerGroup` prefetch was removed, but the surrounding comment still says "This is not mandatory to preload ruler rules, but it improves the UX ... doesn't need to wait for each group to be loaded" and the array is still named `cacheAndRulerPreload` (lines 81-84). Both now describe behaviour that no longer exists and will mislead future readers about what is being preloaded.

findings.title: Test codifies the loss of Pause/Delete actions and drops provisioned-rule coverage
findings.body: `expect(menuItems.length).toBe(4)` asserts that only silence/copy-link/duplicate/export exist, locking in the fact that Pause and Delete are no longer reachable from the Grafana rule list (see AlertRuleMenu's `rulerRule` gates). There is also no test covering a provisioned rule (`provenance` set on the prom DTO) to verify that mutating actions stay hidden, which is now the only mechanism preventing destructive actions on provisioned rules in this view.
